request.spec:
Add an audit viewer to the screen: a filter entry, a show button and a list of lines. With the
filter blank it lists every audit line of this sheet exactly as the file holds it, newest first.
With a name in the filter it lists only the lines about that person: those carrying name=<the
name> or person=<the name>, compared as names are compared (case and surrounding spaces ignored).
The viewer reads what the file holds; it is not a second record.

agent.result_text:
I added the audit viewer and all 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**Server**
- `Audit.java` has a new `lines()` method that reads the audit file as it is now. Nothing new is stored or written, so the viewer only reads the file and is not a second record.
- A new `audit` package holds `AuditViewService` and `AuditViewController`, which answer `POST /api/audit/list` with `{sheet, name}`:
  - It keeps only lines whose second field is exactly `sheet=<id>`, unchanged from the file, newest first.
  - When a name is given, it keeps only lines with `name=<name>` or `person=<name>`, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. The name has to be the field's whole value: what follows it must be the end of the line or the next `key=` field. So "Ada" doesn't match "Adam", and names containing spaces still work.

**Front end**
- A new `AuditView` component in `features/audit/audit-view.ts` has the filter entry (`audit-filter`), the show button (`audit-show`) and the list (`audit-line` items). It sits in the People screen after the void-reasons section.
- Pressing Show clears the old list before fetching, so two presses that give the same lines can still be told apart. Only the latest press's answer is shown, and the list is cleared when a sheet is loaded again.
- I also added an error element (`audit-error`) for a failed read. The spec doesn't use it.

The viewer shows lines regardless of the "as of" date and doesn't check the user's role, so anyone signed in can read the whole audit for a sheet. The request didn't ask for limits there; tell me if you want them.
